geometry_edits.rationale: Soften the dominant axis bend to reduce blockiness while preserving a single readable massing gesture.
Turn the courtyard toward the verified access side to create a legible public threshold.
Expand the carve so the void becomes a real spatial figure rather than a small notch.

graph_edits.rationale: Make the dominant mass less box-like and better oriented toward a continuous neighborhood gesture.
Reduce the arbitrary stepped/blocky feeling and keep a calmer, more coherent primary mass.
Align the public void with the verified access side so the ground edge can read as an entry court rather than an internal subtraction.
Enlarge the void slightly so it becomes a meaningful public/open-space figure in plan and section.
Keep the protected threshold logic but shift it to better expose the ground plane at the access edge.

rationale: The candidate is coherent across the four views and clearly occupies the parcel, but the mass reads as a generic stacked box with only a modest carved/terraced response. The dominant gesture is legible, yet it is not strongly tied to the verified access edge: the blue frontage edge does not resolve into a clear public void, court, undercut, or entry seam. The top view suggests a courtyard-like notch, but it is small and semantically weak relative to the whole. Programmatically, neighborhood living wants an active ground threshold and a meaningful public or semi-public void; this form gestures toward that, but the section remains too blunt and the access response is underdeveloped. The mass also risks reading as an arbitrary stepped object rather than a capacity-aware neighborhood block with a clear street relationship. Reference precedents point toward stronger courtyard/terrace integration, bridge-like connections, and more expressive section continuity.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: The reference is more pavilion/cultural than a compact neighborhood living block, so use its courtyard/bridge logic rather than its specific silhouette.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A compact mass with a large central void and a clear bridge-like upper connection can support neighborhood/public program well.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Much larger multi-building composition than this candidate; do not imitate the scale or tower-campus relationship.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Courtyard-centered campus-like massing with stepped/terraced low-rise blocks can create hierarchy and public open space.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: More open and porous than the candidate; avoid assuming the same degree of perimeter transparency.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: An elongated low-rise mass with a carved central void and horizontal roof logic can keep the ground active.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: The reference is more distributed and landscape-driven; the candidate currently reads too blocky to inherit this fully.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Terraced/ribbon-like section and connected wings around a court can produce a coherent neighborhood collective mass.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: This reference is more complex and multi-winged; the candidate lacks comparable sectional variety and entry articulation.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Interlocking volumes with a substantial courtyard and void-under-block condition can express public threshold and hierarchy.

warnings: Parcel containment appears acceptable; no hard-gate violation from the visible massing.
The access edge is under-responded to: the frontage remains mostly sealed rather than publicly articulated.
The silhouette is coherent but still too box-like and only lightly carved for the stated neighborhood-living brief.
